acceptanceCriteria: A build-log entry inventories every path where host- or model-produced output enters Corvint evidence, evaluation or learning, with the file and function for each.
Each path is classified as having an explicit output-class policy (accept, abstain, refuse) or not, with a ticket filed for each gap; V1-0369 is cross-referenced.
The entry records whether every buffer or history on those paths has a byte or token bound, citing the code.
body: Filed 2026-10-04 from the owner's request to learn from claude-mem (github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem, shallow clone at bfc50259f64a, 2026-10-03). Its plans/18-observer-response-pipeline.md documents silent data loss because every non-conforming LLM reply fell into one bucket that confirmed the claimed batch: prose instead of XML, auth/model/transport errors arriving as assistant text, context overflow, empty replies, schema drift, and a hard-coded max_tokens truncating 76% of responses; history buffers were also unbounded. Their remedy is one explicit classifier with one policy table mapping each output class to {preserve batch | confirm batch | abort with reason}, plus a budget on every history and buffer. Corvint mostly avoids LLM-authored evidence, but some paths ingest host or model output: daily-loop and harness task observations (open V1-0369 is an instance: the cost gate accepts unmatched and failed task observations as savings), doccompiler admission of generated documentation, and any learning inputs. Question: is there a single inventory of these ingestion points, and does each refuse or abstain on an unrecognised output class instead of accepting it?
title: Spike: classify every model- or host-produced output before it becomes Corvint evidence or a learning input
